segments.dry: Most reviewers with dry skin, including one whose skin was dry and sensitized by cold weather, report the cleanser leaves skin moisturized and balanced rather than tight or stripped; one reviewer cautions it isn't deeply hydrating and that those prone to extreme dryness may want a richer cleanser.
segments.combination: One reviewer with combination skin found it gentle and suitable for sensitive skin generally, but noticed her skin could feel a little dry with regular use.
segments.sensitive: The large majority of reviewers who identify as having sensitive, reactive or easily irritated skin report no redness, stinging or tightness and describe the cleanser as calming and non-stripping; one reviewer with dermatitis is a strong exception, reporting that it flared her eye-area dermatitis, inflamed her whole face and left it covered in spots, which she attributes to the niacinamide or the coconut-derived surfactants.

concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers, including several with dry or sensitive skin, report the cleanser leaves skin moisturized, calm and never tight or stripped; dissenting voices include a combination-skin reviewer who found it a little drying with regular use, one who calls it not deeply hydrating for very dry skin, and the reviewer whose barrier reaction left her skin inflamed.
concerns.redness: Many reviewers report no redness after use, including some describing calmer-looking redness with regular use; one reviewer with dermatitis is the exception, reporting her whole face became inflamed after a few days of use.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers describe the cleanser as protecting or supporting the skin barrier without stripping it, and one cites its approval by the National Eczema Association; one reviewer with dermatitis reports the opposite, that it 'wrecked' her skin barrier and triggered a flare, which she attributes to the niacinamide or coconut-derived surfactants in the formula.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers, including some who describe themselves as acne-prone, report no new breakouts; two reviewers dissent, one who broke out worse after use and one whose skin became inflamed and covered in spots during a reaction she attributes to the formula.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer noted her T-zone became noticeably oilier by midday when using this cleanser and settled on using it only as a nighttime step for that reason; no other reviewer in this set describes an oiliness concern.

aspects.libelle: Good value, goes a long way

extraits.texte: I'll add the correct ingredient list to the end of my review. This cleanser seems like it would be gentle. It is low lather and has a decent ingredient list, on paper. However, it flared my dermatitis around my eyes and wrecked my skin barrier after a few days of use. My whole face got inflamed and covered in spots. It also smells like feet. I think the niacinamide caused the flares, so if you're sensitive to that (I've used it fine in the past but I think my skin is getting intolerant of it as of late) this is probably not a good option. Also not a good option if you are sensitive to coconut derived surfactants or alternative preservatives. Anyway, here's the ingredients: AVENE THERMAL SPRING WATER (AVENE AQUA), GLYCERIN, WATER (AQUA), COCO-GLUCOSIDE, SODIUM COCOYL GLUTAMATE, ALGIN, CITRIC ACID, GLYCERYL OLEATE, GLYCOL DISTEARATE, HELIANTHUS ANNUUS (SUNFLOWER) SEED OIL (HELIANTHUS ANNUUS SEED OIL), HYDROGENATED VEGETABLE GLYCERIDES CITRATE, NIACINAMIDE, SODIUM BENZOATE, TOCOPHEROL, XANTHAN GUM.
